def load() -> pd.DataFrame:
    import numpy as np
    # Re-read the raw file to parse properly
    rows = []
    with open('data/astronomy/input/omni2/omni2_Kp_Index.lst', 'r') as f:
        for line in f:
            parts = line.strip().split()
            if len(parts) >= 4:
                year = int(parts[0])
                doy = int(parts[1])
                hour = int(parts[2])
                kp = float(parts[3])
                rows.append({'year': year, 'doy': doy, 'hour': hour, 'Kp': kp})
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    # Build datetime
    df['datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(df['year'].astype(str) + df['doy'].astype(str).str.zfill(3), format='%Y%j') + pd.to_timedelta(df['hour'], unit='h')
    return df

def process(load_swarm) -> pd.DataFrame:
    import numpy as np
    df = load_swarm.copy()
    # CDF epoch: ms since 0 AD (Jan 1, year 0)
    # Unix epoch: ms since Jan 1, 1970
    # Offset = 62167219200000 ms (1970 years * 365.25 days * 86400 s * 1000 ms)
    time_ms = df['time'].values
    offset_ms = 62167219200000
    unix_ms = time_ms - offset_ms
    dt = pd.to_datetime(unix_ms, unit='ms', utc=True).tz_convert(None)
    df['datetime'] = dt
    df2 = df[['datetime', 'a_cal_0', 'flag_val', 'flag_thr']].copy()
    df2.loc[df2['a_cal_0'] > 1e3, 'a_cal_0'] = np.nan
    return df2

operators.customDisplayName: Parse Swarm CDF data: convert CDF epoch (ms since 0 AD) to UTC datetime by subtracting offset to Unix epoch, extract along-track calibrated acceleration (a_cal_0), replace fill value 9999 with NaN. Returns datetime + a_cal_0 + flag columns at 1-second resolution.

def process(parse_swarm) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = parse_swarm.copy()
    # Only use good quality data (flag_val==0)
    df = df[df['flag_val'] == 0].copy()
    df['datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(df['datetime'])
    df['hour'] = df['datetime'].dt.floor('H')
    hourly = df.groupby('hour')['a_cal_0'].mean().reset_index()
    hourly.columns = ['datetime', 'a_cal_0']
    return hourly

def process(merge_data) -> pd.DataFrame:
    from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
    from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error
    import numpy as np

    df = merge_data.copy()
    df = df.sort_values('datetime').reset_index(drop=True)

    # Create 3-hour ahead target: target at hour H is a_cal_0 at hour H+3
    # Feature at hour H predicts target at hour H+3
    # So X[i] = feature[i], y[i] = a_cal_0[i+3]
    lag = 3
    n = len(df)  # 24

    X_kp   = df['Kp'].values[:n - lag].reshape(-1, 1)
    X_pdyn = df['Pdyn'].values[:n - lag].reshape(-1, 1)
    y      = df['a_cal_0'].values[lag:]  # targets shifted 3 hours ahead

    # 70/30 train-test split on the 21 samples
    split = int(len(y) * 0.7)  # 14 train, 7 test

    X_kp_train,   X_kp_test   = X_kp[:split],   X_kp[split:]
    X_pdyn_train, X_pdyn_test = X_pdyn[:split], X_pdyn[split:]
    y_train, y_test           = y[:split],       y[split:]

    # Model 1: Kp
    m1 = LinearRegression().fit(X_kp_train, y_train)
    pred_kp = m1.predict(X_kp_test)
    rmse_kp = np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_test, pred_kp))

    # Model 2: Pdyn
    m2 = LinearRegression().fit(X_pdyn_train, y_train)
    pred_pdyn = m2.predict(X_pdyn_test)
    rmse_pdyn = np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_test, pred_pdyn))

    return pd.DataFrame({
        'model': ['Kp', 'Pdyn'],
        'rmse': [rmse_kp, rmse_pdyn],
        'n_train': [split, split],
        'n_test': [len(y_test), len(y_test)],
        'coef': [m1.coef_[0], m2.coef_[0]],
        'intercept': [m1.intercept_, m2.intercept_]
    })

operators.customDisplayName: Fit two single-variable linear regression models to predict Swarm Alpha along-track acceleration (a_cal_0) 3 hours ahead. Uses 3-hour lag: X[i] predicts y[i+3]. 70/30 train-test split on 21 usable pairs (first 14 train, last 7 test). Model 1: Kp input; Model 2: Pdyn input. Reports RMSE on test set for both models.
